abstract: Purpose: In Posterior Segment Eye Diseases (PSEDs), the homeostatic relation between retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and retina is disrupted. A better understanding of the transcriptomic changes occurring in different ocular cell types can help to elucidate disease mechanisms. Currently, there is no complete detailed workflow describing the process of simultaneous RNA isolation from RPE and retina separately. In this paper, our aim was to develop an easy, reproducible protocol for simultaneous isolation of RNA from both murine RPE and retina. Methods: We developed an efficient and straightforward workflow for isolating RNA from both murine RPE and retina simultaneously. We described the method in detail spanning from mouse euthanasia to downstream RNA analysis. We compared the efficiency of this isolation method between different mice strains (C57BL/6 vs BALB/c). Results: Our method provided high yield of RNA from both RPE and retina across different strains. We observed better quality of RPE RNA in terms of A260/130 ratios in C57BL/6 mice. The retinal RNA quality and yield were comparable across both strains. Beta-catenin immunofluorescent staining also validated our success of RPE removal in the choroidal flat-mounts in both strains. Conclusions: We described an improved workflow for obtaining RNA simultaneously from both RPE and retina. We compared the efficiency of our process via multitude of downstream analyses across different mice strains. Translational Relevance: This method will be beneficial to understand the RPE or retinal tissue specific mRNA transcript changes in preclinical mice models of PSEDs.
